_about: Third-party material no package manager knows about. Read by scripts/notices.mjs and shown on docs/guide/code-use.md and in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Each entry was checked against the repository on 2026-11-20; add an entry in the same change that introduces the material, and remove it in the change that removes it. 'use' is one of: container image, separate process, font files, copied source, linked library.

entries.name: Node.js (official Docker image node)
entries.license: MIT (Node.js; its LICENSE also lists bundled libraries under their own licences); image build files MIT (nodejs/docker-node); the image also contains Debian bookworm packages under their own licences
entries.licenseEvidence: Node.js LICENSE (https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/LICENSE, and the same file in a Node 22 install) opens 'Node.js is licensed for use as follows:' followed by the MIT text and a list of externally maintained libraries; nodejs/docker-node LICENSE is MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2015 Joyent, Inc.'
entries.notes: Build and run stages of the web app image.

entries.name: Python (official Docker image python)
entries.license: PSF-2.0 (Python); image build files unverified; the image also contains Debian packages under their own licences
entries.licenseEvidence: Python's LICENSE.txt (in a Python 3.13 install) contains 'PYTHON SOFTWARE FOUNDATION LICENSE VERSION 2'; the image's Docker Hub page points to that licence information for Python 3 and states the image contains other software under other licences. The licence of the docker-library/python build files could not be read (GitHub rate limit) and is unverified.
entries.notes: Base image of the planner service.

entries.name: pgvector (Docker image pgvector/pgvector)
entries.licenseEvidence: pgvector LICENSE (https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector/blob/master/LICENSE): 'Portions Copyright (c) 1996-2026, PostgreSQL Global Development Group ... Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software and its documentation for any purpose, without fee, and without a written agreement is hereby granted', the PostgreSQL Licence text. pgvector's Dockerfile builds FROM postgres:$PG_MAJOR-$DEBIAN_CODENAME, so the image also contains the PostgreSQL entry below and Debian trixie packages under their own licences.
entries.notes: The db service. The extension is loaded by the database server; the web app talks to it over the network.

entries.name: PostgreSQL
entries.licenseEvidence: https://www.postgresql.org/about/license: 'PostgreSQL is released under the PostgreSQL License, a liberal Open Source license, similar to the BSD or MIT licenses.' The licence of the official postgres image's build files (docker-library/postgres) was not read.
entries.notes: Runs as its own container; the web app connects to it over the network through the pg client library.

entries.name: pgvector (Docker image pgvector/pgvector, CI only)
entries.licenseEvidence: Same project and licence file as the pgvector entry above.
entries.notes: Database service for the test job in GitHub Actions; not part of what is shipped.

entries.name: UI components (Button, Dialog, Input, Table, Card, StatusBadge)
entries.license: owner's own work (Planet9V/eigenia); four files follow shadcn/ui's structure (MIT)
entries.licenseEvidence: The owner stated on 20 November 2026 that all six components come from Eigenia, his own project (Planet9V/eigenia). button.tsx, dialog.tsx, input.tsx and table.tsx describe themselves as 'shadcn/ui ... themed to Eigenia's design tokens'; shadcn/ui is published under the MIT License ('Copyright (c) 2023 shadcn', https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/LICENSE.md). Card.tsx and StatusBadge.tsx carry no third-party note.
entries.origin: Planet9V/eigenia, the owner's own project (owner's statement, 20 November 2026)
entries.changes: Re-themed to Eigenia design tokens (per the file headers). On 20 November 2026 button.tsx gained the variant and size names shadcn/ui components pass, and dialog.tsx gained DialogHeader.

entries.name: shadcn/ui components added by its CLI
entries.version: as fetched by `npx shadcn@latest add` on 2026-11-20
entries.origin: https://ui.shadcn.com registry, written into this repository by the shadcn CLI
entries.changes: None. The files are as the CLI wrote them; colours come from the theme variables in src/app/globals.css.

entries.name: Graphviz (apt package graphviz)
entries.version: as installed by apt in the planner image (Debian)
entries.license: EPL-1.0 (Graphviz; the Debian package also contains libraries under their own licences)
entries.licenseEvidence: Graphviz licence page https://graphviz.org/license/ : Graphviz is distributed under the Eclipse Public License 1.0. Debian package copyright file lists the components. Not re-read in this session; check before release.
entries.notes: Installed with apt in the planner image. WireViz runs the dot command as a separate process to draw the harness. Never linked into the app.

entries.name: occt-import-js (OpenCascade STEP reader, WebAssembly)
entries.version: as copied from the npm package occt-import-js
entries.license: LGPL-2.1 (the package and OpenCascade Technology, per the LICENSE.md copied with it)
entries.licenseEvidence: public/vendor/occt/LICENSE.md is the GNU LGPL version 2.1 text shipped in the package. Whether the combined wasm is LGPL-2.1 only or LGPL-2.1 with the OCCT exception was not checked; the owner should confirm.
entries.origin: npm package occt-import-js, copied into public/vendor/occt so the browser can load it from the same origin
entries.changes: None. The files are as the package ships them (about 7.6 MB of wasm).

entries.name: WireViz (Python package, run as a command)
entries.licenseEvidence: WireViz repository LICENSE (https://github.com/wireviz/WireViz) is GPL-3.0; not re-read in this session.
entries.notes: planner/harness.py starts the wireviz command as a subprocess and reads its svg and bom files. It is never imported, so the GPL-3 code is not linked into the planner or the app.
